_comment: Role -> backend map. `Local & Hybrid Hosting Plan.md` §4 specifies this as
config, not code: 'one entry per logical role, each pointing at a backend',
'overridable per-scene without touching engine code, the same way a World
Pack swap doesn't touch engine code'.
EDIT THIS FILE, NOT THE ENGINE, to change which model serves a role.
The split follows call volume, per §4: high-volume/lower-judgment stays
local; low-volume/high-judgment goes to the cloud tier. The cloud tier is
CLAUDE CODE as of 2026-08-17 (Matt: 'as we build it, Claude through Claude
Code needs to be the model'), not Gemini -- that key was deleted and is
being revoked at the provider. The gemini backend stays defined and unused.

actor_draft._why: §4: highest call volume in the turn loop -- 2-3 alts, per Actor, every turn. Never route this to a subprocess-per-call backend.

table_read._why: §4: a cheap, low-stakes setup check by design.

director_arbitration._why: §4: nuanced judgment, called once per take rather than once per alt.

continuity_classify._why: §7/§8: runs only after the deterministic graph walk narrows the candidate set.

manuscript_compile._why: §10: prose-level judgment in chapter-sized chunks; the plan reserves the stronger tier for exactly this.
